subject: Linguistics
title: Grammaticality Judgments
description: A quick, practical guide to Grammaticality Judgments.

hook.text: 'Colorless green ideas sleep furiously.' It's nonsense—but it sounds like valid English.

buildup.text: Speakers can judge whether a sentence follows syntactic rules regardless of its meaning.

discovery.text: Chomsky used this famous sentence to show that syntax is independent from semantics.

twist.text: Ungrammatical strings like 'furiously sleep ideas green colorless' feel instantly worse.

climax.text: This intuition proves that speakers encode abstract structural rules, not just word associations.

punchline.text: You know the structure is right even when the meaning is absurd.

quiz.question: What did Chomsky's 'colorless green ideas' example prove?
